Heading into the game, the Eagles had deliberately planned to manage Barkley's workload to some extent, but he ended up seeing fewer snaps than anticipated after his back locked up on him following a 29-yard run in the first quarter. He didn't end up taking any snaps after the third quarter, with the Eagles leaning exclusively on Dameon Pierce (undisclosed) and Elijah Mitchell out of the backfield over the final 15 minutes. He helped spearhead five consecutive scoring drives to start the second half, capping four of them with touchdown passes to Mike Gesicki (six yards), Tee Higgins (13 yards), Ja'Marr Chase (two yards ) and Drew Sample (16 yards). The game marked Burrow's second straight with four scoring tosses and zero interceptions, and both his passing yardage total and 73.3 percent completion rate were his second highest of the season. He'll take 1,653 passing yards and a 15:3 TD:INT into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

Sampson is the clear No. 2 RB when the Browns' backfield is at 100 percent, but there could be enough volume for Sampson to have fantasy value in that role given the team's fairly underpowered aerial attack. Sampson will look to stay productive in Week 8 against the Steelers.

items.summary: Coleman led the team in carries in his return from injured reserve and finished second behind Bo Nix (73) in rushing yards. J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey combined for just 29 rushing yards on nine rushing attempts, though Dobbins had a rushing touchdown and Harvey had a receiving touchdown. Coleman was notably the team's running back of choice as the Broncos ran out the clock in the fourth quarter, and head coach Sean Payton said after the game that the team has "got to get (Coleman) more touches," per Aric DiLalla of the Broncos' official site. Denver will likely continue to utilize all three running backs in Week 8 against the Chiefs, but this was an encouraging performance for Coleman in the rookie fourth-round pick's first action since Week 2.

items.headline: Goff completed 22 of 32 passes for 303 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Packers.
items.summary: It's the third time in six games this season Goff has passed for 300-plus yards, and the fifth time he's tossed multiple TDs. Both of his scores in this one went to Jameson Williams, as he connected with the speedy wideout for a 16-yard strike in the first quarter and a 10-yard touchdown in the third. Goff will take a stellar 14:0 TD:INT into a crucial NFC North battle in Week 8 against the undefeated Vikings.

items.headline: LaPorta caught one of two targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Packers.
items.summary: It wasn't a happy Tight Ends Day for LaPorta, who had his worst performance of the season despite the fact that Jared Goff threw for over 300 yards. Even with the quiet afternoon, LaPorta still sports a 28-334-3 line on 39 targets through six games, keeping him on pace for a new career high in receiving yards. He faces another tough challenge in Week 8 versus the dominant defense of the undefeated Vikings.

items.headline: Lions' Dan Campbell downplays Sam LaPorta's contract comments
items.summary: Lions coach Dan Campbell is downplaying comments made by Sam LaPorta about the tight end's displeasure with where contract talks stand with the organization. LaPorta later softened the tone on his comments.

items.headline: Sam LaPorta not feeling contract 'love' from Lions ahead of 2027 free agency
items.summary: Tight end Sam LaPorta, who will be a free agent after the season, expressed some frustration that the Lions are "not showing the love" and indicated he would be OK with playing elsewhere in 2027.

items.headline: Harrison caught one of four targets for a six-yard touchdown in Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: In his second game since being acquired from Arizona via trade, Harrison scored his first touchdown with the Texans. His six-yard touchdown catch in the second quarter was Harrison's lone catch in a game during which six different wide receivers recorded at least one reception for the Texans. Harrison will have an opportunity to increase his knowledge of the playbook during a Week 8 bye and potentially earn more playing time in Houston's crowded wide-receiver room.

items.headline: Inside Marvin Harrison Jr.s' exit from the Cardinals
items.summary: Harrison never reached his potential in Arizona, but all sides are hoping for a fresh start moving forward.

items.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. will play for Texans on Sunday in London, coach says
items.summary: Texans wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. will play against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday, Houston coach DeMeco Ryans said Wednesday.

items.headline: Dell caught his only target for 43 yards and added a two-yard rush during Sunday's 27-21 overtime loss to the Giants.
items.summary: Dell made his return to action after missing nearly two full years while recovering from a dislocated kneecap and a series of torn ligaments in his left knee. The wide receiver was on the field for only 11 offensive plays, but he made the most of his one target. Dell reeled in a deep ball from C.J. Stroud in the second quarter, churning out a 43-yard gain. With Nico Collins, Marvin Harrison, Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel (toe) and Kayshon Boutte also in the mix at wide receiver, Dell may have a hard time getting many looks each week.

items.headline: Texans' Tank Dell says he won't fear being hit in return Sunday against Giants
items.summary: Texans WR Tank Dell said he is "ready to get tackled" on Sunday when he returns for his first game since suffering a gruesome knee injury in December 2024.

items.headline: Texans WR Tank Dell to play Sunday in 1st game since major 2024 knee injury
items.summary: Texans wide receiver Tank Dell will return to the field against the New York Giants on Sunday after a 22-month hiatus.

items.headline: Adams (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports.
items.summary: As a result, Adams is slated to miss at least four games, although Ian Rapoport of NFL Network previously suggested that the wideout was hoping to return not too long after the Rams' Week 11 bye. In his absence, Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield and Tutu Atwellare candidates to see added looks behind top WR Puka Nacua.

items.headline: Rams suffer several major injuries, including to WR Adams, who's out 6-10 weeks
items.summary: Rams wideout Davante Adams ruptured a hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Cardinals, and he will be sidelined for six to 10 weeks, coach Sean McVay announced.

items.headline: Caleb Douglas proves he's the Dolphins' top receiver

items.headline: Douglas (ankle) caught two of three targets for 70 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Douglas made an immediate impact in his first action since Week 2. The rookie third-round pick capped the game's first drive with a seven-yard touchdown catch for his first NFL TD, then stayed in along the sideline to score again on a 63-yard catch-and-run in the fourth quarter. Miami utilizes a run-heavy approach when possible, but the Dolphins may be forced to throw more if they fall behind as expected in Week 8 against the Patriots, which could lead to more opportunities for Douglas.

items.headline: Dolphins rookie WR Caleb Douglas set to return vs. Jets

items.headline: Vikings RB Jones avoids serious knee injury, day-to-day
items.summary: Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. avoided a serious knee injury Sunday and is considered day-to-day, coach Kevin O'Connell confirmed Monday.

items.headline: The left knee injury that forced Jones out of Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts isn't considered significant, and the running back is viewed as day-to-day, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports.
items.summary: Jordan Mason (thumb) returned from injured reserve and stepped back in as the Vikings' lead ball carrier while Jones shifted into a change-of-pace role. Jones carried eight times for 26 yards and added one reception for no gain across 15 snaps before exiting with 12:22 remaining in the fourth quarter. After the game, head coach Kevin O'Connell acknowledged that Jones experienced an aggravation of the MCL sprain he previously sustained in Week 2. Jones was able to return to action the following week, but the results of an MRI on Monday will help determine whether he can avoid an absence during the Vikings' Week 8 game in Detroit.

items.headline: Vikings praise Aaron Jones Sr.'s heart with Jordan Mason out
items.summary: Jones said he was proud knowing the team was counting on him and he "can still be an every-down productive back."

items.headline: Mason carried the ball 15 times for 68 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Colts. He failed to catch either of his two targets.
items.summary: Making his return from an IR stint due to a thumb injury that had kept him out since Week 1, Mason ended up leading the Vikings in rushing yards after Aaron Jones aggravated a knee injury and spotted in and out of the lineup. Jones had been getting a hefty workload while Mason was sidelined, but their roles could be reversed in Week 8 against the Lions.

items.headline: Vikings activate RB Jordan Mason off injured reserve

items.headline: Doubs (shoulder) is hopeful to return after the Patriots' Week 11 bye and isn't expected to face a long-term absence, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports.
items.summary: With Doubs already on injured reserve, this report offers a more encouraging timeline after Sunday's shoulder injury. He'll still need to miss at least four games, but a possible return after the bye would keep the Patriots from being without one of their key wide receivers for an extended stretch. Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be in line for increased snaps alongside A.J. Brown and slot man DeMario Douglas with Doubs sidelined.

items.headline: Patriots' Romeo Doubs hurt on 42-yard TD catch vs. Jets
items.summary: WR Romeo Doubs was hurt after diving to haul in a 42-yard touchdown pass from Drake Maye with 4:10 remaining in the first quarter.

items.headline: Nabers caught seven of nine targets for 111 yards in Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans.
items.summary: The switch from Jameis Winston to J.J. McCarthy at quarterback for the Giants hasn't slowed Nabers down at all, and the team's No. 1 wideout extended his streak of games with over 100 receiving yards to four. During that surge, Nabers has delivered a 36-509-2 line on 51 targets, as he puts his injury-marred sophomore NFL campaign firmly behind him. He'll try to not to lose his momentum during the bye before facing the Eagles in Week 9.

items.headline: Hall (quadriceps) is inactive for Sunday's Week 7 matchup against the Dolphins.
items.summary: Early Sunday reports indicated Hall was unlikely to play, and a fourth straight absence for the star running back is now official. With Hall sidelined again Sunday, Braelon Allen, who's averaged 18.3 carries, 84.3 rushing yards, 1.7 receptions and 11.3 receiving yards over the past three games while serving in the lead role, once again will helm the Jets' ground attack. Meanwhile, Hall will target a return to action in a Week 8 home matchup against the Raiders next Sunday.

items.headline: Jets WR Adonai Mitchell to play, RB Breece Hall questionable vs. Dolphins
items.summary: Jets WR Adonai Mitchell, sidelined four games with a finger injury that required a surgical procedure, practiced all week and will play against the Dolphins.

items.headline: Jets rookie WR Omar Cooper Jr. to return vs. Patriots; RB Hall, WR Mitchell out
items.summary: Jets rookie wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) will play against the Patriots, but running back Breece Hall and wideout Adonai Mitchell have been ruled out for Sunday's game.

items.headline: Eagles' DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks out vs. Cowboys
items.summary: The Eagles' top two receivers -- DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks -- have been ruled out of Monday night's game against the Cowboys.

items.headline: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Cowboys.
items.summary: Smith was unable to practice all week while nursing a hamstring injury, and the Eagles will be without both of their top wide receivers, as Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) has also been ruled out. Rookie Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown figure to be the Eagles' top wideouts for Monday night's game, and tight end Dallas Goedert will be a go-to target for quarterback Tanner McKee due to the absences of both Smith and Wicks. Smith's next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Commanders on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: Eagles' Saquon Barkley ruled out; DeVonta Smith likely to return
items.summary: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers with a hamstring injury, but it appears WR DeVonta Smith will return.

items.headline: Darnold completed 20 of 28 passes for 257 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Chiefs. He added two rushing attempts for 17 yards.
items.summary: Darnold threw a 28-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the second quarter to give the Seahawks a 10-0 lead, but Darnold's end-zone interception from the 3-yard line in the final minute of the first half allowed the Chiefs to stay within striking distance. Seattle's dominant defense made sure Darnold's eighth interception in five starts since returning from a glute injury wouldn't prove too costly. He has matched that interception total with eight touchdown passes over that span. Darnold and the 4-3 Seahawks will play at home in prime time again Week 8, hosting the Bears on MNF.

items.headline: Seahawks sticking with Sam Darnold as starter despite INTs

items.headline: Seahawks' Sam Darnold owns up to late interceptions in overtime loss to Broncos

items.headline: Daniels was back in his primary reserve role behind Baker Mayfield in Sunday's 43-13 win over the Panthers.
items.summary: Daniels entered Sunday's contest late in the fourth quarter with Tampa Bay in full command of the contest, ultimately recording minus-3 rushing yards while kneeling on back-to-back plays to end the game. With Mayfield back in action, Daniels now will have to wait for his next chance to command the Buccaneers offense.

items.headline: Bucs QB Jalon Daniels swaps jerseys with idol, Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers
items.summary: Following Pittsburgh's 26-19 overtime victory, Jalon Daniels left with a keepsake from his idol, Aaron Rodgers.

items.headline: Mayfield to practice this week but Buccaneers to prep as if Daniels will play
items.summary: Baker Mayfield will return to practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers, but the team will prepare as if Jalon Daniels will start at QB, coach Todd Bowles said.

items.summary: The Washington Commanders placed running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve, sidelining their starting back for at least four games.

items.headline: The Commanders placed Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve Monday.
items.summary: Croskey-Merritt had already been ruled out for Monday's game against the 49ers, but his move to IR ensures that he'll miss at least an additional three contests beyond that. With Croskey-Merritt sidelined through Week 10, Rachaad White looks on track to serve as the Commanders' top option out of the backfield in the interim, while Austin Ekeler and Jeremy McNichols are on hand in complementary roles.

items.headline: Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt out vs. 49ers with groin injury
items.summary: Commanders running back Jacory Croskey-Merritt won't play against the 49ers because of a groin injury, coach Dan Quinn said.

items.headline: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin has torn patellar tendon, ending his season
items.summary: Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin suffered a torn patellar tendon, an injury that will end his season, coach Dan Quinn announced Tuesday.

items.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn announced Monday that McLaurin has been diagnosed with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee following an MRI and will miss the rest of the season.
items.summary: McLaurin went down with the injury on the Commanders' second possession of Monday's 23-17 loss to the 49ers. With McLaurin out of the mix for the rest of 2026, Stefon Diggs profiles as the Commanders' top wideout, while players such as Chig Okonkwo, Antonio Williams, Treylon Burks, Dyami Brown and Rachaad White could see their roles in the passing game expand further. McLaurin, who is under contract with Washington through 2028, finishes the season with 230 receiving yards and a touchdown on 15 receptions over five games.

items.headline: Commanders' Terry McLaurin carted off with knee injury in MNF loss to 49ers
items.summary: Terry McLaurin was carted off the field with his left leg in an air cast after injuring his knee against the 49ers. He'll undergo additional testing Tuesday.

items.headline: Bourne caught three of six targets for nine yards during Sunday's 30-16 loss versus the Broncos.
items.summary: Coming off the heels of a second straight five-catch game, Bourne had positive momentum heading into Week 7. However, while his six targets were encouraging, his production was less efficient than a team baseline that was already not very good. With that said, teammate Jalen Brooks suffered a season-ending wrist injury Sunday, leaving Bourne as the Cardinals' undisputed second option at wide receiver moving forward.

items.headline: Facts vs. Feelings: Out of Love with Jeremiyah, but another Cardinal looms
items.summary: Why Jeremiyah Love is a bust candidate but Kendrick Bourne is a sleeper, and more Week 6 lineup insights.

items.headline: The Cardinals placed Brooks (wrist) on injured reserve Tuesday.
items.summary: The transaction comes after Brooks announced earlier in the day that he underwent season-ending wrist surgery. Brooks saw light snaps through the first four weeks of the season, but he stepped in as the Cardinals' No. 3 wideout for the past three games after Marvin Harrison was traded to the Texans. The 26-year-old will finish the 2026 campaign with five receptions for 81 yards on 17 targets to go with 499 yards on 19 kickoff returns.

items.headline: Cardinals WR Jalen Brooks to miss rest of season with wrist injury
items.summary: Cardinals wide receiver Jalen Brooks posted on social media Monday that he will miss the rest of the season with a wrist injury.

items.headline: Dalton (coach's decision) is inactive for Sunday's game against the 49ers, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports.
items.summary: Dalton is a healthy scratch for Sunday's contest as he continues to ramp up his participation in the Falcons' offense. The quarterback joined the team after being cut by the Eagles on Oct. 9. Jack Strand (coach's decision) will be the inactive QB behind Michael Penix and Tua Tagovailoa for Week 7 against the 49ers.

items.headline: Falcons sign veteran QB Andy Dalton, release QB Cooper Rush
items.summary: The Falcons have signed veteran quarterback Andy Dalton and released quarterback Cooper Rush, the team announced on Monday.

items.headline: Robinson rushed 20 times for 63 yards and brought in all five targets for 59 yards in the Falcons' 29-20 win over the 49ers on Sunday.
items.summary: As his rushing line suggests, Robinson was mostly held in check by a stout 49ers front. The All-Pro running back's longest run of the day went for only 12 yards, but Robinson did find a way to make up some of the fantasy production as a receiver. Robinson finished tied for second in receptions and targets while checking in as the runner-up in receiving yards for the Falcons on the afternoon, and his numbers in the first two categories were his second highest of the campaign. Robinson has seen a downturn in opportunity and production since rushing for 339 combined yards in Weeks 3 and 4, and he'll look to reverse that trend in a Week 8 road matchup against a tough Buccaneers run defense next Sunday.

items.headline: Coleman brought in four of six targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Bills' 33-30 win over the Raiders on Sunday.
items.summary: Coleman led the Bills in receiving yards on the afternoon with the help of a 21-yard grab and a 12-yard touchdown reception with just over six minutes remaining in the third quarter. The score was Coleman's third of the season, with the previous two having come in each of the prior pair of contests against the Patriots and Rams. The oft-maligned 2024 second-round pick appears to be picking up some momentum in his third season, as Coleman already has a 19-283-3 line on 24 targets while helping make up for the multiple absences of DJ Moore (shoulder).

items.headline: Kincaid (ribs) returned to Sunday's 33-30 win at Las Vegas and finished with seven catches (on eight targets) for 38 yards.
items.summary: Kincaid missed some time from late in the third quarter and into the fourth to be evaluated in the sideline tent, but he got back on the field with 8:01 remaining and added one more reception to his final line. Overall, he paced the Bills in catches and targets, but he ended Week 6 with his lowest YPC (5.4) of the campaign. The Bills have a Week 7 bye, so he'll have plenty of time to heal up for Buffalo's next game Sunday, Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

items.headline: Fantasy football Week 6 inactives: Jeremiyah Love, DJ Moore out
items.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.

items.headline: Moore (shoulder) is listed as inactive Sunday in Las Vegas.
items.summary: After sitting out a Week 5 overtime win at the Rams, Moore managed just one limited practice (Friday) this week, and he donned a red non-contact jersey while doing so. Per Joe Buscaglia of The Athletic, Moore again didn't log much activity during pregame warmups for a second straight week, forecasting another absence was likely. With Moore's status now clarified, Khalil Shakir, Keon Coleman and Joshua Palmer (shoulder) should earn most of the WR reps in the Bills offense in Week 6.

items.headline: Etienne posted six carries for eight yards, reeled in both targets for 17 yards and compiled 69 kickoff-return yards during Sunday's 43-13 defeat to the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Etienne made his second appearance of the 2026 campaign after missing the first four games due to an ankle injury. Although he was slightly more productive than he was in the Week 6 win over the Eagles, it was still an underwhelming showing overall. Etienne should continue to occupy the No. 2 spot on the depth chart. However, Chuba Hubbard is anticipated to nearly monopolize the touches out of the backfield moving forward, leaving sparse opportunity for anyone else.

items.headline: Taylor Moton among 3 Panthers activated ahead of Eagles game
items.summary: The Panthers will have RT Taylor Moton and DE Tershawn Wharton available Sunday against the Eagles. RB Trevor Etienne was also activated off IR.

items.headline: Tremble hauled in one of two targets for eight yards during Sunday's 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers.
items.summary: Tremble had two touchdowns in the 25-14 win over the Eagles in Week 6. However, it was a different story in Week 7, with the 26-year-old catching just one pass for the second time this season. While Tremble could find the end zone again at some point moving forward, he likely won't be consistent enough to be considered anything other than a desperation fantasy option, especially while Darren Waller is on the field.

items.headline: Panthers' Tremble admits TD taunt was payback for 'suplex' by Eagles' DeJean
items.summary: Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble apologized for costing his team a penalty after he taunted defensive back Cooper DeJean, saying it was retaliation for an earlier personal foul.

items.headline: Bears RB Kyle Monangai (toe, thumb) out Thursday vs. Patriots
items.summary: The Bears have ruled RB Kyle Monangai out for Thursday night's matchup against the Patriots with lingering toe and thumb injuries.

items.headline: Monangai (toe/thumb) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Patriots.
items.summary: Monangai thus will miss a third game in a row as he tends to a turf toe injury. Last Friday, head coach Ben Johnson told Courtney Cronin of ESPN.com that the Bears aren't expecting to place Monangai on injured reserve, so he appears to have a chance to return in Week 8 at Seattle next Monday, assuming he's able to get back on the practice field next week. In the meantime, D'Andre Swift will continue to lead Chicago's backfield, with Roschon Johnson on hand as Swift's top backup.

items.headline: Is Chase Brown still a starting fantasy RB?
items.summary: Is Chase Brown still a starting fantasy RB?

items.headline: Brown rushed 11 times for 39 yards and brought in four of five targets for 19 yards in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
items.summary: Brown didn't partake in the Bengals' five-touchdown second-half explosion, but the versatile back had a serviceable day on a per-touch basis. However, Brown hasn't really come close to reaching the 100-yard mark on the ground in any game this season -- the closest he's come is 80 yards -- and he's been at 61 yards or fewer in five of six contests. Brown's pass-catching work continues to typically be plentiful, but he still has a relatively modest outlook heading into a Week 8 home matchup against the Titans next Sunday.

items.headline: Chase's fiery halftime speech inspires Bengals to comeback win vs. Ravens
items.summary: Ja'Marr Chase unloaded on his Bengals teammates in a halftime speech that inspired Cincinnati to a comeback victory over the Ravens.

items.headline: Chase brought in five of seven targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 35-13 win over the Ravens on Sunday.
items.summary: Chase played a clear second fiddle to Tee Higgins, who had a team-high 148 receiving yards, as the former finished second to his teammate in receptions and receiving yards while tying him for the team lead in targets. Chase also recorded a touchdown grab for the second straight game, bringing in a two-yard scoring strike from Joe Burrow at the halfway point of the fourth quarter. Chase is still in search of his first 100-yard game of the season, and he'll look to break the ice on that front in a Week 8 home matchup against a vulnerable Titans secondary next Sunday.

items.headline: Bengals put TE Erick All Jr. on IR; believed to be torn ACL, per source
items.summary: Bengals put TE Erick All Jr. on injured reserve Tuesday with an injury that's believed to be a torn ACL, a source told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

items.headline: The Bengals placed All (knee) on injured reserve Tuesday.
items.summary: Though All will be eligible to return from IR as soon as Week 12, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network relays that the third-year tight end is feared to have sustained a season-ending ACL tear of his right knee during Sunday's 35-13 win over the Ravens. All will likely undergo further testing over the next day or two before the Bengals provide an updated diagnosis, but if the ACL tear is confirmed, the 26-year-old could be sidelined into the 2027 season. He previously tore the ACL in the same knee in 2023 during his final collegiate season at Iowa and during his 2024 rookie campaign with Cincinnati.

items.headline: The Browns activated Gabriel (back) from injured reserve Monday.
items.summary: Cleveland needed to make a decision on the quarterback after opening his 21-day practice window 20 days ago, so he'll now join the 53-man roster as one of the team's four quarterbacks. The Browns figure to make a move at the position in the near future, and perhaps they'll try to gauge trade interest in Gabriel.

items.headline: Browns activate Gabriel off IR, now have 4 QBs on roster
items.summary: The Browns activated quarterback Dillon Gabriel off injured reserve Monday, giving the team four passers on the 53-man roster.

items.headline: Jeudy caught all four of his targets for 21 yards during Sunday's 27-24 win at Tennessee.
items.summary: Jeudy now has four catches in each of his last two games, an encouraging sign after he had no more than three in any of the first five games of the season. He's still trailing rookies Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in terms of playing time, however. Jeudy is not on the radar in most formats going into a Week 8 matchup at Pittsburgh.

items.headline: Jerry Jeudy, amid trade buzz, has clutch catch in Browns' win, gets game ball
items.summary: Browns wide receiver Jerry Jeudy had a clutch catch in Cleveland's game-winning drive Sunday, earning a game ball from coach Todd Monken.

items.headline: Judkins carried the ball 17 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans. He also caught his only target for eight yards.
items.summary: Making his return from an ankle injury that sidelined him in Week 6, Judkins put together his best performance of the season, punching in red-zone TDs from five yards out in the first quarter and six yards out in the second. His 96 rushing yards and 104 scrimmage yards were also season highs. Judkins will try to keeping rolling in Week 8 against the Steelers.

items.headline: Browns RBs Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson expected to play
items.summary: The Browns' top two running backs, Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson, are expected to play against the Titans after being sidelined with injuries.

items.headline: Browns balance relishing close wins, lamenting slow starts
items.summary: Despite a "complete game" by Deshaun Watson, offensive struggles are still lingering for the AFC North-leading Browns.

items.headline: Watson completed 25 of 36 passes for 308 yards with an interception in Sunday's 27-24 win over the Titans. He added 19 yards and a touchdown on three carries.
items.summary: While he didn't throw a TD pass for a second straight game, Watson produced a season high in passing yards and scored his first rushing TD since Week 2 of the 2024 season on a nine-yard scamper in the fourth quarter. Watson also led his fifth game-winning, fourth-quarter drive of the year, completing another comeback after the Browns fell behind 14-0 early. The veteran QB will take a 7:3 TD:INT through seven games into a Week 8 meeting with the Steelers.

items.headline: Pickens brought in four of six targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
items.summary: Pickens tied for second in receptions and finished third in receiving yards on the night for the Cowboys, and the athletic receiver added his second touchdown of the season on a highly difficult catch in the right corner of the end zone with just under six minutes remaining in the second quarter. Both of Pickens' scoring grabs this season have come in the last three games, and he's now boasting a 37-485-2 line on 58 targets as a Week 8 home matchup against the Cardinals approaches this Sunday.

items.headline: George Pickens makes excellent use of his fingertips with TD grab
items.summary: George Pickens makes excellent use of his fingertips with TD grab

items.headline: Turpin (ribs) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Eagles, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
items.summary: Turpin was held out of practice all week due to a rib injury that he picked up against the Packers this past Sunday. He'll miss his first game of the regular season, and his absence means Tyler Goodson and Jonathan Mingo will likely serve as the Cowboys' returners on kickoffs and punts. Turpin's next opportunity to play is Week 8 against the Cardinals on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: Cowboys returner KaVontae Turpin injures rib on opening kickoff; X-rays clean
items.summary: Cowboys Pro Bowl returner Turpin sustained a rib injury on his opening kickoff return after he was tackled awkwardly. X-rays were clean, according to coach Brian Schottenheimer.

items.headline: Williams rushed 25 times for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 38-21 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
items.summary: Williams broke out for a new single-game career high in rushing yards during the impressive victory, sealing the win with a two-yard scoring run just ahead of the two-minute warning in the fourth quarter. The remarkable performance also marked Williams' first 100-yard tally of the season, and he's been highly rewarding for fantasy managers by scoring a touchdown in five straight games. Williams should have a prime opportunity to continue building on his strong first half of the season in Week 8, as he'll face a vulnerable Cardinals run defense at home on Sunday.

items.headline: Javonte Williams waves bye after scoring a TD for Dallas
items.summary: Javonte Williams waves bye after scoring a TD for Dallas

items.headline: Is Courtland Sutton back on the flex radar?
items.summary: Is Courtland Sutton back on the flex radar?

items.headline: Sutton caught three of five targets for 45 yards during Sunday's 30-16 win over Arizona.
items.summary: Sutton was able to reel in three passes for the first time since Week 3, and his 45 receiving yards were his second highest total in a contest this year. The wide receiver has had an overall disappointing campaign so far, but Jaylen Waddle (chest) exited the contest in the fourth quarter, so Sutton could be thrust into a more prominent role in Week 8 against the Chiefs.

items.headline: Waddle didn't return to Sunday's 30-16 win over the Cardinals due to a chest injury, Parker Gabriel of the Denver Post reports.
items.summary: Waddle went to the locker room in the fourth quarter, and the Broncos confirmed shortly before the end of the game that he was dealing with a chest injury. Sunday's injury could be an aggravation of the chest injury that bothered Waddle in practice leading up to the game. Waddle is likely to pop up on the injury report as the Broncos prepare for a Week 8 rematch with the Chiefs, who defeated Denver in Week 1. He finished with four catches for 48 yards on seven targets against the Cardinals.

items.headline: Where is Jaylen Waddle? Broncos' big offseason acquisition is off to slow start
items.summary: With just 204 receiving yards through five games, Jaylen Waddle has been mostly contained and hasn't yet made the impact the Broncos hoped. What has gone wrong?

items.headline: Montgomery (groin) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports.
items.summary: Montgomery still hasn't returned to practice and will miss a second straight game, leaving Woody Marks to handle a large workload against the Giants. Jawhar Jordan (quad) was effective off the bench last week, but he's now on the practice-squad injured list, which leaves Dare Ogunbowale as the No. 2 RB. Ogunbowale's history as a special teamer and passing-down specialist suggest Marks should dominate carries.

items.headline: Texans RB Montgomery, S Pitre out for London affair vs. Jaguars
items.summary: Texans starting RB David Montgomery (groin) and safety Jalen Pitre (shoulder) have been ruled out for Sunday's matchup against the Jaguars in London.

items.headline: Is Seth McGowan a worthwhile add in fantasy football?
items.summary: Is Seth McGowan a worthwhile add in fantasy football?

items.headline: McGowan turned 11 carries into 46 yards, caught his only target for two yards and added 140 yards as a kick returner during Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Vikings.
items.summary: McGowan played a season-high 31 percent of the team's offensive snaps, and as a result, he was able to set new highs in both carries and rushing yards. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded in the coming weeks, the rookie would stand to operate as the team's lead back following Taylor's departure. On the season, McGowan has rushed 34 times for 134 yards and reeled in four of five targets for 12 yards while compiling 566 kickoff-return yards over seven contests so far.

items.headline: Colts QB Anthony Richardson Sr. charged with possession of marijuana
items.summary: Colts quarterback Anthony Richardson Sr. is facing a misdemeanor charge for marijuana possession following a traffic stop earlier this month, court records show.

items.headline: Richardson was charged with misdemeanor possession of marijuana in Carmel, Indiana earlier this week, Tyler Haughn of FOX 59 reports.
items.summary: It means very little, and Richardson will likely face no punishment from the NFL. He'll continue to serve as Daniel Jones' backup.

items.headline: Colts' Tyler Warren to miss second game with groin injury
items.summary: Tight end Tyler Warren will miss his second consecutive game with a groin injury when the Colts travel to face the Vikings on Sunday.

items.headline: Warren (groin) is ruled out for Sunday's game against the Vikings, FOX59's Mike Chappell reports.
items.summary: After missing practice throughout the week, Warren will sit out a second straight game. Will Mallory figures to take over as the team's top pass catcher at tight end, with Mo Alie-Cox and Drew Ogletree also having roles.

items.headline: Travis Hunter stars in Jaguars' loss, is 1st with INT and TD catch since 2002
items.summary: The Jaguars' Travis Hunter had a historic day at Wembley Stadium, becoming the first player since 2002 to record an interception and TD catch in the same game.

items.headline: Hunter caught all four of his targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans in London. He also recorded three tackles and an interception.
items.summary: The two-way player is beginning to flash the talent that made him the second overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft. Hunter's receiving numbers were by far a season high -- he had only two catches coming into Sunday -- and his day on offense was capped by a seven-yard touchdown reception from Trevor Lawrence in the fourth quarter that brought the Jaguars to within a field goal at 31-28. Hunter then made an impact on the very next possession, picking off a C.J. Stroud pass in the end zone with just under four minutes left on the clock to keep his team in the game. The touchdown and interception were each the second of his career in his 13th NFL game, and Hunter became the first player since 2002 to have one of each in the same game. Jacksonville's receiver room is crowded with Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Brian Thomas at the top of the depth chart, but head coach Liam Coen hinted after the game that Hunter's role on offense could continue to grow following the team's Week 7 bye, per CBS 47 Jacksonville.

items.headline: If Brian Thomas Jr. is traded, could it boost his fantasy value?
items.summary: If Brian Thomas Jr. is traded, could it boost his fantasy value?

items.headline: Thomas didn't haul in either of his two targets during Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans in London.
items.summary: Per Michael DiRocco of ESPN.com, Thomas logged 15 offensive snaps in the first half but none after halftime, while all of fellow wideouts Parker Washington (11 targets), Jakobi Meyers (10) and Travis Hunter (four) had major roles in the Jaguars offense. Thomas maintained a regular workload in the first five games of the season, with his snap shares ranging from 35 to 62 percent en route to a 9-105-1 line on 18 targets. Sunday's development could be a sign of things to come for Thomas without the team mentioning any sort of injury during or after Sunday's contest.

items.headline: How should fantasy managers view Bhayshul Tuten moving forward?
items.summary: How should fantasy managers view Bhayshul Tuten moving forward?

items.headline: Tuten carried the ball 12 times for 39 yards and caught all four of his targets for 48 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
items.summary: While the Houston front seven kept him bottled up on the ground -- Tuten's longest run went for just five yards -- the second-year RB made an impact through the air, turning a dump pass from Trevor Lawrence into a 27-yard score in the second quarter before catching another two-yard TD before halftime. The receiving touchdowns were his first of the season and tied his total from all of 2025, and Tuten topped 80 scrimmage yards for the fourth straight game. The Jaguars will get a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

items.headline: Washington caught four of 11 targets for 64 yards in Sunday's 34-31 loss to the Texans.
items.summary: Despite leading the Jaguars in targets, Washington finished second to Jakobi Meyers in both catches and receiving yards, and he wasn't on the other end of any of Trevor Lawrence's four TDs. It's the third time in the last four games that Washington has failed to reach five grabs or 70 yards, but the fourth contest featured a 6-124-2 line from the fourth-year wideout. Washington will take a 26-416-4 line on 46 targets into a bye before facing the Colts in Week 8.

items.headline: Jaguars WR Parker Washington has the clutch gene: Will that earn him an extension?
items.summary: Did you see Washington's one-handed grab in London? How did he get so good at contested catches? And how did he quickly become a big part of the Jaguars' offense?

items.headline: Kelce caught four of eight targets for 44 yards in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Kelce increased his career total to 1,104 regular-season catches, passing Hall of Famers Marvin Harrison (1,102) and Cris Carter (1,101) to move up to fifth on the all-time list. Jason Witten holds the fourth spot with 1,228 receptions, so Kelce is more likely to be caught by Keenan Allen (1,084) than Kelce is to catch Witten. Kelce led the Chiefs with eight targets in the absence of WR Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) and tied fellow TE Noah Gray for the team lead in receiving yards as Kansas City mustered just three Harrison Butker field-goal attempts on offense, two of which missed. This was only the second time Kelce failed to reach the 50-yard threshold in six appearances this season. He had 71 yards in Week 1 against the Broncos, whom the Chiefs will face in a Week 8 road rematch.

items.headline: Mahomes and Kelce the Chiefs dynamic duo
items.summary: Mahomes and Kelce the Chiefs dynamic duo

items.headline: Rice (hamstring) will be out for Sunday's game at Seattle, Sam McDowell of The Kansas City Star reports.
items.summary: With Rice set to miss another game, the Chiefs are left with Xavier Worthy as their top wide receiver. Rice still hasn't returned to practice and thus seems in danger of missing time beyond Week 7.

items.headline: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice out Sunday vs. Chargers with hamstring injury
items.summary: Kansas City's top receiver Rashee Rice will miss Sunday's game against the Chargers with a right hamstring injury.

items.headline: Worthy caught three of six targets for 11 yards in Sunday's 20-3 loss to the Seahawks.
items.summary: Seattle successfully limited Worthy's output in the absence of Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee), with the versatile Nick Emmanwori running stride for stride with the speedy Worthy on a couple of downfield misconnections. Worthy finished second behind Travis Kelce (eight) in targets but sixth on the Chiefs in receiving yards Sunday. Heading into a Week 8 road game against the Broncos, Worthy has drawn at least six targets in five of six games this season. He has reached 70 yards twice and failed to eclipse 25 yards in any of the other four games.

items.headline: Kansas City Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy thriving in expanded role as Seahawks loom
items.summary: The Chiefs will likely need similar improved play -- or even better -- from Worthy in Sunday's showdown vs. Seattle.

items.headline: Kirk Cousins to remain Raiders' starting QB vs. Jets, Klint Kubiak says
items.summary: Kirk Cousins will remain the Raiders' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Jets, coach Klint Kubiak announced Monday.

items.headline: Head coach Klint Kubiak said that Cousins will remain the Raiders' starting quarterback heading into Sunday's game against the Jets, Paul Gutierrez of the team's official site reports. "There is no controversy," Kubiak said. "He is playing at a very high level."
items.summary: Though the Raiders have dropped four straight games to drop to 3-4 on the season, Kubiak reaffirmed his commitment to Cousins, who has done his part to keep the team competitive amid the losing streak. The veteran signal-caller leads the NFL with 16 touchdown passes and ranks third with 1,877 passing yards, with the Raiders' struggling defense (28.1 points allowed per game) and poor running game (3.0 yards per carry) having been the bigger culprits in the team's recent swoon. According to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Kubiak said that No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza is "going to play at some point," but the rookie looks like he'll have to wait at least one more week before seeing extended action while Cousins has directed a serviceable offense.

items.headline: Jeanty rushed eight times for 15 yards and brought in all eight targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
items.summary: The Rams stonewalled Jeanty on the ground, but the 2025 first-round pick was highly effective as a receiver. Jeanty led the Raiders in receptions and tied for second in targets, and his 15-yard grab came when the running back ran past Kam Curl down the right sideline early in the fourth quarter. Jeanty has been held under 30 rushing yards in three straight games, but he's up to a 34-312-3 receiving line on 44 targets going into a Week 8 road matchup against the Jets next Sunday.

items.headline: Raiders' Ashton Jeanty feels 'great' ahead of game vs. Bills
items.summary: Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty, who has been battling ankle and foot injuries, said he's feeling great ahead of Sunday's game against the Bills.

items.headline: Mendoza did not appear in Sunday's 35-21 loss to the Rams.
items.summary: Mendoza didn't see any action for the second straight week after he got his toes wet in the team's Week 5 loss to New England. With the Raiders falling to 3-4 with the loss in Week 7, current starting quarterback Kirk Cousins may not remain in that role for much longer. Las Vegas will travel to face the Jets in Week 8 before a trio of tough matchups against the 49ers, Seahawks and Broncos in the ensuing three weeks.

items.headline: Fernando Mendoza is embracing being Raiders' latest Hispanic QB
items.summary: The rookie's next chapter is inspired by the legacies of a Hispanic coach, QB and a Raiders' fan base embracing the culture.

items.headline: Tucker secured five of 12 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders' 35-21 loss to the Rams on Sunday.
items.summary: Tucker led the Raiders in receiving yards and targets on the afternoon with a big lift from a game-long 41-yard catch and a 37-yard fourth-quarter touchdown reception. The speedy wideout has a combined 10-200-3 line over his last two games alone as he continues to take his chemistry with Kirk Cousins to new levels, and Tucker is averaging a stellar 16.3 yards per reception heading into a favorable Week 8 road matchup against the Jets next Sunday.

items.headline: Fantasy football last-minute pickups: Winston, Tucker among top options
items.summary: If injuries, bye weeks or tough matchups have you seeking lineup help, Matt Bowen lists potential options.

items.headline: Hampton rushed seven times for 18 yards and caught all four of his targets for 21 yards in Sunday's 22-6 loss to the Chiefs.
items.summary: The Chargers continued to deloy an ineffective backfield rotation, as Hampton got 11 touches compared to 10 for Kimani Vidal and two for Keaton Mitchell. None of the three running backs exceeded 3.0 yards per carry while QB Justin Herbert led the team with 26 rushing yards. Hampton has been trending in the wrong direction, with his rushing yardage dropping with each subsequent game since a 94-yard performance on the ground in Week 2 against the Raiders. He'll look to reverse that trend in Week 8 against the Rams following a Week 7 bye.

items.headline: Why is Chargers RB Omarion Hampton's snap count decreasing?
items.summary: Coach Jim Harbaugh and OC Mike McDaniel on why RB Omarion Hampton is being used differently.

items.headline: McConkey (concussion) was spotted on the field in a no-contact jersey during the Chargers' bonus practice session Monday, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: After a Week 7 bye, the Chargers held an unofficial practice Monday as they begin prepping for a road matchup with the Rams next Sunday. Though the team won't have to release its first Week 8 injury report Wednesday, McConkey appears poised to be listed as at least a limited practice participant, which suggests that he's made some progress through the five-step concussion protocol. The wideout will look to practice fully by the end of the week and receive clearance from an independent neurologist in order to play against the Rams.

items.headline: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey ruled out with concussion vs. Chiefs
items.summary: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey, in his first action since injuring his foot in Week 4, left Sunday's game early after suffering a concussion in the second quarter.

items.headline: National Tight Ends Day 2026: Davis Allen, Mason Taylor put on a show during holiday
items.summary: The fourth weekend in October means National Tight Ends Day, and the NFL's tight ends made sure to bring their best.

items.headline: Allen caught four of five targets for 20 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 35-21 win over the Raiders.
items.summary: With Davante Adams (hamstring) and Terrance Ferguson (ankle) sidelined for the Rams, Allen was thrust into an elevated role on offense for Los Angeles. He ended up running just 12 routes on Matthew Stafford's 32 dropbacks but made the most of his chances, particularly in the red zone, where Allen caught three- and five-yard touchdowns in the first half. Allen's volume of routes isn't enough to make him a reliable fantasy option moving forward.

items.headline: Williams rushed 16 times for 99 yards and a touchdown and brought in both targets for 22 yards in the Rams' 35-21 win over the Raiders on Sunday. He also lost a fumble.
items.summary: Williams logged one fewer carry than Blake Corum but outgained his teammate by six yards, and although the former's lost fumble came at the Rams' 30-yard line, it didn't lead to any Raiders points. Williams scored his fifth rushing touchdown of the campaign on a 17-yard run late in the first half, and he fell a yard short of his first 100-yard effort of the season. Despite the division of labor in a game that yielded a run-friendly game script, Williams should remain the clear leader of the ground attack in a Week 8 home matchup against the Chargers next Sunday.

items.headline: Kyren Williams says Rams' inconsistencies on offense 'probably' due to role
items.summary: Asked why he thought the Rams' energy level was inconsistent from drive-to-drive Sunday, RB Kyren Williams said: "Probably because I'm not out there."

items.summary: Why fantasy managers should be excited about Greg Dulcich

items.headline: Dulcich caught all five of his targets for 86 yards in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Dulcich led the Dolphins in catches, receiving yards and targets as Miami notched its first win of the season. The 2022 third-round pick of the Broncos is still searching for his first touchdown of the season after scoring once in 10 games for the Dolphins in 2025. Dulcich is likely to remain a key target for Malik Willis in Week 8 against the Patriots.

items.headline: Willis completed 14 of 21 passes for 208 yards and two touchdowns while rushing six times for 39 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 28-25 win over the Jets.
items.summary: Willis gave the Dolphins their first lead of the season with a seven-yard touchdown pass to Caleb Douglas on the opening drive. After the Jets tied the game on the ensuing possession, Miami reclaimed the lead with a one-yard Ollie Gordon touchdown run, and Willis extended the advantage to 14 points with a two-yard touchdown run in the waning seconds of the first half. Miami's offense stalled for most of the second half until Willis found Douglas for a 63-yard catch and run to take a 28-17 lead with 4:44 remaining in the fourth quarter. The Jets scored on their next drive, but Willis sealed his first win as Miami's QB with a successful fourth-down QB sneak to pick up a first down and set up victory formation. Up next for Willis and the 1-5 Dolphins is a Week 8 home game against the Patriots.

items.summary: Why Hunter Henry is a top TE streamer in Week 8

items.headline: Henry secured all seven targets for 71 yards in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
items.summary: The veteran tight end was a key contributor throughout the night, finishing with team-high figures in receptions and targets while ending second in receiving yards. All three components of Henry's receiving line also were season-high figures, and he now has between 44 and 71 receiving yards in four consecutive games. Henry will take a 26-296-2 line on 31 targets into a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: Is Drake Maye a top-5 fantasy QB?
items.summary: Is Drake Maye a top-5 fantasy QB?

items.headline: Maye completed 24 of 31 passes for 321 yards with two touchdowns and one interception while adding four rushes for 26 yards and another score in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
items.summary: Maye's final line was one that could have easily been generated in victory, but the 2024 first-round pick couldn't quite help the Patriots keep pace with the high-powered Bears offense. Nevertheless, he was able to post his second 300-yard effort in the last three games, while also tossing multiple touchdowns for the fourth straight contest. Maye connected with Rhamondre Stevenson and Eli Raridon from 48 and 30 yards, respectively, for those two scoring strikes, the former coming off a screen pass on the last snap of the first half. Those big plays were preceded by Maye's seven-yard scoring run early in the second quarter, and he also pulled his season completion rate up to 65.9 percent with Thursday's highly efficient effort. The third-year signal-caller should have a good opportunity to stay hot in a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards and brought in all five targets for 93 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots' 30-24 loss to the Bears on Thursday.
items.summary: Stevenson had another tough day on the ground, especially considering he gained 13 of his 22 yards on one carry. However, the veteran back had a standout performance as a receiver, leading the Patriots in receiving yards on the night with a big hand from a weaving 48-yard touchdown catch off an end-of-half screen play. Stevenson is now averaging just 3.7 yards per carry across the first seven games of the campaign, but he's up to a 20-204-1 receiving line on 24 targets heading into a Week 8 road matchup against the Dolphins on Sunday, Nov. 1.

items.headline: Things you don't know about Patriots running back Rhamondre Stevenson
items.summary: Stevenson does all the little things for the Patriots, and he's on the cusp of 100 carries for the sixth straight season.

items.headline: Miller rushed eight times for six yards in Sunday's 16-10 loss to the Steelers in Paris.
items.summary: The Saints got absolutely nothing going on the ground against Pittsburgh, rushing 17 times for 18 yards as a team, so it's not like Miller and his team-leading eight carries was the only issue. New Orleans heads into its bye in Week 8, and Travis Etienne (hamstring) will be eligible to come off injured reserve for Week 9 against the Browns. When both Etienne and Alvin Kamara were healthy and active together earlier this season, Miller was a healthy inactive.

McCarthy inserted under center for his first start with the Giants, Likely took a big hit in production, as Malik Nabers led the team in targets (nine), catches (seven) and yards (111) despite the tough on-paper matchup with cornerback Derek Stingley. items.headline: Giants place RB Tyrone Tracy Jr. on IR with hamstring injury
items.summary: The Giants are placing RB Tyrone Tracy Jr. on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, with Devin Singletary expected to play a bigger role on offense.

items.headline: Singletary carried the ball five times for 41 yards and a touchdown and caught all three of his targets for 14 yards in Sunday's 27-24 overtime win over the Texans.
items.summary: Attrition may have helped solve the Giants' backfield mess, at least in the short term. Tyrone Tracy left the game in the second quarter with a hamstring injury and didn't return, and Cam Skattebo may also have picked up a hamstring strain on his final tote of the day, a 42-yard dash in OT that set up a 30-yard TD run for Singletary that won the game. A well-timed Week 8 bye could allow both RBs to avoid missing any further time, but if either or both are still on the shelf on the other side of the break, Singletary could wind up handling a much bigger role in Week 9 against the Eagles.

items.headline: The Giants placed Tracy (hamstring) on injured reserve Tuesday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.
items.summary: Just as general manager Joe Schoen indicated would be the case earlier in the day, Tracy was deactivated after straining his hamstring during Sunday's 27-21 overtime win over the Texans. He'll be out for at least the next four games, making the Giants' Week 13 game against the 49ers his earliest possible return date. While Tracy is sidelined, Devin Singletary is expected to operate as the top complement to Cam Skattebo (hamstring), who thrived while moving back into a lead role out of the backfield in the Week 7 victory.

items.summary: The Giants are placing RB Tyrone Tracy Jr. on injured reserve with a hamstring injury, with Devin Singletary expected to play a bigger role on offense.

items.headline: Allen rushed 17 times for 104 yards and caught six of seven targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
items.summary: Allen worked as the lead back for a fourth consecutive game, as Breece Hall (quadriceps) was ultimately inactive after being listed as questionable heading into the game. The 235-pound Allen continued to struggle in short yardage, getting stuffed on a goal-line attempt in the fourth quarter as the Jets were denied a game-tying touchdown and instead settled for a field goal to cut the deficit to four points with 8:57 remaining. Allen has exceeded 100 rushing yards twice during Hall's absence but has just one touchdown over that span and two touchdowns this season. Hall worked ahead of Allen prior to getting hurt, but they may split the backfield workload more evenly if Hall's cleared to return against the Raiders in Week 8.

items.headline: Why Derrick Henry has taken Jets RB Braelon Allen under his wing
items.summary: After Henry saw Allen wearing his shirt in college, he reached out to him, and the two running backs have kept in touch since.

items.headline: Jets' Garrett Wilson says sideline screaming wasn't directed at Geno Smith
items.summary: Garrett Wilson said he was just expressing frustration after cameras caught the Jets star WR screaming on the sideline during a disappointing loss to Miami.

items.headline: Smith completed 23 of 30 passes for 287 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins. He also rushed twice for no gain and threw a successful two-point conversion.
items.summary: Smith matched Miami's opening-drive touchdown with a 13-yard touchdown pass to Mason Taylor on the Jets' first drive, but the veteran QB threw an interception deep in Dolphins territory on the next drive. The Jets trailed for the entirety of the last three quarters, allowing Smith to rack up some big numbers during their failed comeback bid, as he posted his second three-touchdown performance of the season. He found Omar Cooper for a three-yard touchdown in the third quarter after they connected for a 60-yard gain earlier on that drive, and Smith threw a 12-yard touchdown and two-point conversion, both to Taylor, to round out the scoring with 3:24 remaining in the fourth. However, the Dolphins ran out the clock from there to drop the Jets to 2-5 heading into a Week 8 home game against the Raiders.

items.headline: National Tight Ends Day 2026: Davis Allen, Mason Taylor put on a show during holiday
items.summary: The fourth weekend in October means National Tight Ends Day, and the NFL's tight ends made sure to bring their best.

items.headline: Taylor caught all five of his targets for 62 yards and two touchdowns while adding a two-point conversion in Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Dolphins.
items.summary: Taylor bookended the scoring for the Jets. He got New York on the board with a 13-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter and rounded out the scoring in the fourth with a 12-yard touchdown reception and the ensuing two-point conversion. The 2025 second-round pick entered Sunday's action with just one touchdown in 17 career regular-season appearances, but Taylor posted the best performance of his young career while outplaying 2026 first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq, who had just one catch for six yards. Taylor will continue to face competition for targets from Sadiq, as well as the wide-receiver trio of Garrett Wilson, Omar Cooper and Adonai Mitchell, in Week 8 against the Raiders.

items.headline: Lemon brought in seven of eight targets for 67 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles' 38-21 loss to the Cowboys on Monday night.
items.summary: Lemon operated as the Eagles' de facto No. 1 receiver on a night where both DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) were sidelined, and the rookie met the moment by posting career- and team-high figures across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets. Lemon rounded out his solid performance by recording his first NFL touchdown catch on a four-yard scoring grab with just under six minutes remaining in the third quarter. Lemon could have another opportunity to spearhead the air attack in a Week 8 road matchup against the Commanders on Sunday night, as both Smith and Wicks may be hard-pressed to get healthy enough to suit up for that contest.

items.headline: Makai Lemon pinballs in for an Eagles TD
items.summary: Makai Lemon pinballs in for an Eagles TD

items.headline: Pierce didn't take the field for either of the Eagles' final two possessions of Monday's 38-21 loss to the Cowboys after sustaining an undisclosed injury with 8:38 remaining in the fourth quarter, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports.
items.summary: Pierce was the second Eagles running back to make an early exit from Monday's contest, as starter Saquon Barkley was held out for the entire fourth quarter while nursing hamstring and back injuries. Before leaving the contest, Pierce carried 14 times for 47 yards and a touchdown while adding a one-yard reception on his lone target. Ahead of their Week 8 matchup with the Commanders, the Eagles will issue their next injury report Wednesday, when the nature of Pierce's health concern as well as the extent of his practice activity will be revealed.

items.headline: Dameon Pierce scurries in for an Eagles TD
items.summary: Dameon Pierce scurries in for an Eagles TD

items.headline: Eagles' DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks out vs. Cowboys
items.summary: The Eagles' top two receivers -- DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks -- have been ruled out of Monday night's game against the Cowboys.

items.headline: Wicks (ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's game versus the Cowboys.
items.summary: Wicks wasn't able to practice in any capacity during Week 7 prep due to an ankle injury and thus will miss his first contest of the campaign. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also sidelined Monday, the Eagles will rely on a receiving corps composed of Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore and Britain Covey, though TE Dallas Goedert (knee) may end up being the favorite target of QB Tanner McKee.

items.headline: Should fantasy managers consider trading Jaylen Warren while his value is so high?
items.summary: Should fantasy managers consider trading Jaylen Warren while his value is so high?

items.headline: Warren carried the ball 18 times for 101 yards and caught three of four targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 16-10 win over the Saints.
items.summary: The 21 touches tied his season high, while Rico Dowdle got 15 as the Steelers went with a ground-heavy game plan. Warren has topped 100 scrimmage yards in four of the last five games, racking up 472 rushing yards and a TD along with a 17-233-1 line on 24 targets during that hot stretch. He'll remain one of the key pieces of the Pittsburgh offense heading into a Week 8 clash at home against a Cleveland defense that Warren recorded 126 combined yards against in Week 4.

items.headline: Steelers place Wilson on IR with finger injury
items.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers placed Roman Wilson on the injured reserve list, their second key receiver lost to injury in as many weeks.

items.headline: Wilson (finger) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Ray Fittipaldo of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports.
items.summary: Wilson already had been ruled out for Sunday's game against Tampa Bay, but the move to IR means that the third-year pro will be required to miss at least four games. Since the Steelers are on a bye for Week 9, the earliest that Wilson can return is Week 11 against the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 22. He joins Michael Pittman (foot) on injured reserve, which leaves rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard as the Steelers' WR2 behind DK Metcalf for the next few weeks.

items.headline: Steelers bring back veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling amid receiver injury woes
items.summary: The Steelers, in need of help at wide receiver with Michael Pittman Jr. and Roman Wilson out because of injuries, signed veteran Marquez Valdes-Scantling on Tuesday.

items.headline: Valdes-Scantling agreed to sign with the Steelers on Monday as a member of the practice squad, Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: Though Valdes-Scantling will begin his time in the organization on the practice squad, he could be a candidate for elevation to the 53-man roster as soon as Sunday, when the Steelers take on the Saints in Paris. The veteran wideout previously made three appearances this season with the Chargers, recording two catches for 22 yards on five targets while logging 79 total snaps.

items.headline: Kirk played 20 snaps on offense but didn't show up in the box score otherwise during Sunday's 29-20 loss to Atlanta.
items.summary: Kirk was activated off injured reserve Saturday and was cleared to make his 2026 debut following a near three-month absence due to a calf injury that he sustained during training camp in July. His 20 offensive snaps were fourth most among 49ers wide receivers, and while he was being eased back into things, his lack of targets was a bit of a let down considering the 49ers were without both Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring). Both of San Francisco's top pass catchers could be back in action following the Week 8 bye, so Kirk's role for Week 9 against the Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 8 is uncertain.

items.headline: 49ers WR Evans, DE Bosa, WR Samuel out vs. Atlanta; WR Kirk may return
items.summary: 49ers receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr., and defensive end Nick Bosa are among a half dozen players who have been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons.

items.headline: McCaffrey is dealing with a mild hamstring strain rather than a quadriceps injury, and the 49ers believe he'll be ready following the team's Week 8 bye, David Lombardi of SF Standard reports.
items.summary: After McCaffrey briefly exited Sunday's loss to Atlanta with what had been described as a thigh issue, this update offers more clarity on the injury and a favorable outlook. The timing of the 49ers' bye gives the veteran running back added recovery time ahead of their next game in Week 9 versus the Raiders, though his practice status will still be worth monitoring once San Francisco returns to work. Kaelon Black will be a priority add off waivers considering CMC's injury history.

items.headline: Why fantasy managers should hold onto Christian McCaffrey
items.summary: Why fantasy managers should hold onto Christian McCaffrey

items.headline: Samuel (hamstring) has a chance to return following the 49ers' Week 8 bye, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports.
items.summary: All three of Mike Evans (Achilles), Samuel and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) are eyeing a Week 9 return against the Raiders, so the 49ers' wide receiver depth chart could look vastly different coming out of the bye. Samuel would likely go back to his part-time role, handling short-area passes and an occasional handoff or two. He's not a particularly exciting fantasy play when Evans, George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) are all healthy.

items.headline: 49ers WR Evans, DE Bosa, WR Samuel out vs. Atlanta; WR Kirk may return
items.summary: 49ers receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr., and defensive end Nick Bosa are among a half dozen players who have been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons.

items.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 150 receiving yards, TD in Seahawks' win vs. Chiefs
items.summary: Jaxon Smith-Njigba wasn't the main story heading into Sunday night's Chiefs-Seahawks matchup -- but he emerged as the game's biggest star, continuing his own historic start by catching nine passes for 150 yards and a touchdown in Seattle's 20-3 win.

items.headline: Smith-Njigba caught nine of 12 targets for 150 yards and a touchdown while rushing twice for 13 yards in Sunday's 20-3 win over the Chiefs.
items.summary: After leading the league in catches, receiving yards and receiving touchdowns through Week 6, Smith-Njigba increased his pace with a season-high 163 scrimmage yards Sunday night. JSN scored his eighth touchdown of the season on a 28-yard catch in the second quarter, with four apiece having been thrown by Sam Darnold and Drew Lock. Smith-Njigba became the sixth player in NFL history to reach 100 receiving yards in six of his team's first seven regular-season games. He led the league in receiving yards last regular season and is showing no signs of slowing down heading into a Week 8 home game against the Bears on MNF.

items.headline: Baker Mayfield returns for Bucs, but WR Emeka Egbuka, RT Luke Goedeke out
items.summary: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield will make his return following a three-game absence, but he will be without his top target in wide receiver Emeka Egbuka.

items.headline: Egbuka (concussion) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Panthers, Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports.
items.summary: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles previously indicated that Egbuka was doubtful to play, but the official designation is more definitive. Chris Godwin, Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson figure to take most of the WR snaps for the Buccaneers this Sunday at Carolina.

items.headline: Irving rushed 24 times for 106 yards and two touchdowns while bringing in one of two targets for four yards in the Buccaneers' 43-13 win over the Panthers on Sunday. He also committed a fumble that stayed with Tampa Bay.
items.summary: Irving put together a vintage performance on the ground on his way to his second 100-yard effort of the season, both which have come within the last three games. The versatile back was surprisingly involved sparsely as a pass catcher, but Irving helped stake the Buccaneers to a commanding lead with four- and one-yard touchdown runs in the first half. It marked Irving's first multi-TD day of the season on the ground, and he'll next take aim at the defense of another divisional opponent in the Falcons at home next Sunday.

items.headline: Why Adam Rank is starting Bucky Irving every week
items.summary: Adam Rank: Bucky Irving one of the most disrespected players in fantasy

items.headline: Commanders excited about WR Antonio Williams
items.summary: John Keim discusses rookie WR Antonio Williams and the opportunity he has to step up for the Commanders.

items.headline: Coach Dan Quinn noted Monday that with Terry McLaurin (knee) out for the season, Stefon Diggs' workload isn't expected to change much, however others, notably Williams, should see added opportunities in McLaurin's looming absence, Nicki Jhabvala of The Athletic reports.
items.summary: McLaurin was forced out of Week 6 action after logging just seven snaps, while Williams ended up recording 45 snaps alongside Diggs (41 snaps), Treylon Burks (37 snaps) and Dyami Brown (33 snaps). In the process, Williams caught three of his four targets for 50 yards in the contest. Following the Commanders' Week 7 bye, the 2026 third-rounder merits fantasy consideration for those who previously rostered McLaurin or are otherwise looking to added some WR depth ahead of the NFL's Week 8 slate.

items.headline: Allgeier rushed eight times for 19 yards and caught all three of his targets for 30 yards in Sunday's 30-16 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: For a second consecutive game, Allgeier led the Cardinals in carries in the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle) but was far less efficient on the ground than Bam Knight. Allgeier has 57 rushing yards on 26 carries (2.2 YPC) during this two-game span compared to 128 rushing yards on 22 carries (5.8 YPC) for Knight over the same stretch. Love should reclaim his spot as the top option in Arizona's backfield once he's cleared to return, and even if that doesn't happen in Week 8 against the Cowboys, Allgeier could start to cede more opportunities to Knight if Allgeier remains inefficient.

items.headline: Beck (back) is inactive but will serve as the emergency third quarterback against the Broncos on Sunday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.summary: Beck was unable to practice Thursday and Friday due to back spasms. He's inactive for Sunday's contest, but as the emergency third quarterback, he would be allowed to play in the event that both Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew left the game due to injury, illness or ejection.

items.headline: Brissett completed 27 of 48 passes for 272 yards and a touchdown while rushing seven times for 16 yards in Sunday's 30-16 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: After failing to score a touchdown in the Week 6 win over the Rams, Brissett and the Cardinals mustered only one touchdown on five trips into the red zone Sunday. Brissett averaged a meager 5.7 yards per pass attempt but inflated his numbers with heavy volume. He has a 3-16 record since taking over as Arizona's starting QB while throwing at least 40 passes in 10 of those 19 starts. Brissett is likely to post a more efficient passing performance in Week 8 against a far more permissive Cowboys pass defense.

items.headline: Higgins caught all three of his targets for 17 yards and made one tackle on kick coverage in the Cardinals' 30-16 loss to the Broncos on Sunday.
items.summary: Higgins played 39 offensive snaps and 17 special-teams snaps in Sunday's contest. The versatile tight end continues to fill a moderate role in the passing game, allowing the Cardinals to continue playing 12- and 13-personnel packages.

items.headline: The Cardinals signed Hull from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday, Tyler Drake of ArizonaSports.com reports.
items.summary: Hull has been signed to continue to fulfill the No. 3 running back role opened by the absence of Jeremiyah Love (ankle). Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight should continue to see nearly all of the offensive action in Week 7 against the Broncos, with Hull providing additional depth if needed.

items.headline: Knight accrued seven carries for 48 yards and reeled in three of five targets for 15 yards during Sunday's 30-16 defeat to the Broncos.
items.summary: With Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined for a second consecutive contest, Tyler Allgeier and Knight again were tasked with manning the Cardinals backfield. Allgeier earned 11 touches to Knight's 10 on Sunday, but the latter out-gained him by 14 yards from scrimmage (63 versus 49). It was the second week in a row in which Knight churned out more yardage than Allgeier on fewer touches, and even if Love is able to return in Week 8 at Dallas, Knight could begin to put himself in position for regular snaps moving forward, if he hasn't already.

items.headline: McBride caught 10 of 13 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 30-16 loss to the Broncos.
items.summary: McBride became the first tight end in NFL history to record 400 regular-season catches in his first five campaigns, bolstering his career total to 406 with 10 grabs Sunday. He scored Arizona's lone touchdown of the game on a seven-yard catch in the third quarter while setting season highs in catches and receiving yards. McBride has recorded at least seven receptions in all seven games this season while scoring four times heading into a Week 8 matchup with a weak Dallas pass defense.

items.headline: Virgil recorded two receptions for 29 yards on five targets in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Lions.
items.summary: A healthy inactive for the first four games of the season, Virgil ended up suiting up for the first time after the Cardinals opted to hold Marvin Harrison out in Week 5 before trading him to the Texans shortly after Sunday's contest concluded. Virgil served as the Cardinals' No. 4 receiver, logging just 13 of 73 offensive snaps but seeing ample involvement during his limited time on the field. While the rookie fifth-round pick out of Texas Tech should be active for the Cardinals on a regular basis moving forward, he's likely to rank behind Michael Wilson, Trey McBride and Kendrick Bourne in the pecking order for targets.

items.headline: Wilson caught four of eight targets for 55 yards in Sunday's 30-16 loss to the Broncos. He also rushed twice for 11 yards.
items.summary: Wilson finished second on the team behind Trey McBride in catches, receiving yards and targets. The fourth-year wideout has drawn at least seven targets in every game this season, but Wilson has exceeded 56 receiving yards only twice in seven tries. Wilson hasn't stepped up since the Cardinals traded away Marvin Harrison, but the upcoming Week 8 matchup with Dallas' beatable secondary creates a potential breakout opportunity for Arizona's No. 1 wide receiver.

items.headline: When asked Monday if Conner (foot) will play this season, coach Mike LaFleur said "potentially," Dani Sureck of the Cardinals' official site reports.
items.summary: It's a typical LaFleur non-answer type of answer. It was reported two weeks ago that Conner was close to practicing, but there's been no indication his 21-day practice window is close to being opened by the Cardinals. There's not much room on the depth chart for another running back that doesn't play special teams in Arizona.

items.headline: Arizona cut Geers (undisclosed) from its injured reserve list Tuesday, Aaron Wilson of KPRC 2 Houston reports.
items.summary: Geers went to the Cardinals' injured reserve list with an undisclosed injury during the preseason, and he'll now go back to free agency unless he's claimed off waivers by another team. The undrafted rookie is still seeking an opportunity to play his first regular-season snaps as a pro.
